issues.description:
Method: Milkable.messageOnMilk()
Problem statement (UML and textual description) declares/describes messageOnMilk() as returning a boolean (UML: "messageOnMilk():boolean" and text: "messageOnMilk() should return true if milking was successful, false otherwise"). The solution repository declares the interface method as String messageOnMilk() and concrete classes (Seal, Goat) implement it returning descriptive Strings (e.g. "Seal <name> is milked"). The template Main also prints m.messageOnMilk() expecting a printable string. This mismatch creates a direct signature conflict: students following the UML/text will implement/expect a boolean-returning method, while the provided solution and example usage use a String-returning method, causing compilation or behavioral confusion and preventing a clear, consistent contract for the interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose a single, consistent return type for Milkable.messageOnMilk() across problem statement, template, and solution. Recommended resolution: update the UML and textual description in the problem statement to declare messageOnMilk():String and change the instruction text to state it should return a descriptive String (e.g. "Seal <name> is milked") so it matches the solution and the example printing in Main. Alternatively, if boolean behavior is desired pedagogically, change the solution interface and all implementations to return boolean and update example usage and tests accordingly. Document the chosen contract clearly in the problem text and the UML.
